Một hình con sóng khắc ở hướng mương. Mộ: A wave shape is carved toward the canal. A leaf shape is carved toward the dirt road. The two marks point to two different places; they are not a curse.
Mặt tây: “Đường nước, tránh khi lũ”. Mặt: West face: “Water road, keep clear in flood”. North face: “To the banyan, follow the cart track”. The northern characters are more heavily covered in moss.
Dưới phiến đá có lỗ nhỏ từng cắm biển đư: Beneath the slab are small holes where wooden way-signs were once set. The signs have been pulled out, but the socket marks still face the high earth bank.
Muốn tới miếu cây đa thì theo dấu lá cây: To reach the banyan shrine, follow the leaf mark on the north face. The wave mark is the way down to the canal, not the way into the forest.
Thủy Tỉnh Ký – Giếng Đá Năm Xưa: Record of the Water Well – The Old Stone Well
Sổ công việc ghi dây gầu, nắp giếng và v: A work ledger recording the bucket rope, the well lid and the position of the stone steps.
THỦY TỈNH KÝ – GIẾNG ĐÁ NĂM XƯA: RECORD OF THE WATER WELL – THE OLD STONE WELL
Bình — keeper of the yard, the water and the tools.
Đồ hỏng phải sửa ngay, không để đấy dọa: Broken things must be mended at once; do not leave them about to frighten people.
Dây từ mép giếng xuống mặt nước được đán: The rope from the well's edge down to the water is knotted three times so the drawer will not lose his grip. The first knot sits at the well mouth, the next two spans down, the last near the bucket.
Nắp giếng bản lề lệch về phía cây gạo. T: The hinge of the well lid is offset toward the kapok tree. In rain the iron pin must be set. Left open, it can make a person slip when running across the yard at night.
Tôi tháo chiếc chốt đồng ở ngoài thành g: I took the bronze pin from the outside of the well wall to mend the bucket. Something else is set deep in the stone below; I did not touch it. After that, Nhài would often look down into the well and cry.
Nắp giếng chưa được sửa. Trời mưa, nếu k: The well lid has not been mended. In rain, if the pin is not set, a person running past may slip.
Bát Cơm Không Tên – Sổ Bếp Của Nụ: The Nameless Bowl of Rice – Nụ's Kitchen Book
Những trang ghi phần cơm, mâm bát và một: Pages recording rice portions, the dish tray, and a portion set aside for the child.
BÁT CƠM KHÔNG TÊN – SỔ BẾP CỦA NỤ: THE NAMELESS BOWL OF RICE – NỤ'S KITCHEN BOOK
Ngày nào cũng phải đủ phần cho người làm: Every day there must be enough for the hired hands; do not take one person's rice to make up another's.
Ở gian trong có năm người làm công ở lại: Five hired hands stayed in the inner room. The rice cooked for them was usually divided into five portions, with the child's portion kept apart in the main house.
Tôi chuẩn bị sáu chiếc bát: năm bát lớn: I set out six bowls: five large bowls for us, one small bowl for Nhài. No one told us what would happen in the basement.
Bình để khăn gần giếng, tôi cất muôi tro: Bình left his cloth by the well, I put the rice paddle away in the kitchen; Quyên dropped her hairpin by the cradle, Thành kept the letter in the ledger, Giáp left his sandals outside the basement door. I remember them in that order.
Trước khi xuống hầm, chúng tôi đã chia l: Before going down to the basement, we divided the letter of accusation into three pieces and hid them separately. We wrote down what we suspected, hoping someone would find it if anything happened.
Ảnh Trung Tàng Ảnh – Những Bóng Mờ: A Photo Within a Photo – The Faint Shadows
Tập giấy kẹp ảnh Polaroid và hướng dẫn q: A bundle holding Polaroid photos and directions for reading reflected shadows.
ẢNH TRUNG TÀNG ẢNH – NHỮNG BÓNG MỜ: A PHOTO WITHIN A PHOTO – THE FAINT SHADOWS
Ảnh cũ không biết nói, nhưng cũng không: Old photographs cannot speak, but neither are they right by nature.
Nếu thấy trong kính có thêm người, hãy n: If you see an extra person in the glass, look at whether the window behind you is open or shut. One shadow may be light; another shadow appears only in the photo.
Một: nhìn trực tiếp. Hai: chụp ảnh tại c: One: look with your own eyes. Two: photograph it on the spot. Three: compare with something fixed. Do not trust one photo and draw a conclusion.
Bé gái đứng bên chiếc nôi, tay cầm búp b: A little girl stands by the cradle, a cloth doll in her hand. The adult behind her is washed out by the light, so the face cannot be seen. In the mirror, that person's wooden hairpin is very clear.
Nếu ảnh và vật chứng khác nhau, ghi cả h: If the photo and the physical evidence disagree, record both. Memory can be pulled askew; a scratch in wood does not know how to lie.

Which side the bolt must be seen from.
Người ở trong không thể tự với tới thanh: A person inside cannot reach the wooden bar outside.
Con nhớ đếm năm ngón tay. Ngón nào cũng: Remember to count five fingers. Each has a name, but no finger must take another's name.
Một tờ sớ có thể trông rất cũ. Nếu nét m: A petition can look very old. If the ink is different, check who wrote it and the pasted paper; do not believe it merely because it lies in a glass case.
Giáp nhắc Nhài: lúc trời mưa, đừng chạy: Giáp reminded Nhài: when it rains, do not run across the yard while the well lid has no pin set.
Mật Tự Người Cũ – Bảng Ký Hiệu: The Old Household's Secret Signs – Table of Marks
Bảng ký hiệu được dùng để đánh dấu trang: A table of signs used to mark the shared petition pages.
MẬT TỰ NGƯỜI CŨ – BẢNG KÝ HIỆU: THE OLD HOUSEHOLD'S SECRET SIGNS – TABLE OF MARKS
Để người đi vắng vẫn biết ai đã ghi, chú: So that anyone away would still know who had written, each of us used a private mark at the foot of the page.
Bình — sóng nước. Anh trông giếng và biế: Bình — water wave. He watched the well and knew the bucket rope.
Nụ — flame. She watched the kitchen.
Quyên — nốt nhạc. Cô dạy Nhài hát khi tr: Quyên — musical note. She taught Nhài to sing when it rained.
Thành — scales. He kept the ledgers and weighed the goods.
Ở sau ảnh tập thể có thứ tự đứng ký. Khô: On the back of the group photo is the order of signing. It is not the order in which people were forced to stand during the rite.
Đừng đọc thứ tự trên cửa hầm thành thứ t: Do not read the order on the basement door as the order of standing for sacrifice. We signed the petition because we wanted out of this place, not because we asked to be shut in again.
